title: CRLR/252/2017 of Balwant Singh Vs State Of Uttarakhand

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 252 of 2017
Balwant Singh Ö..Revisionist
Versus
State of Uttarakhand Ö.Respondents
Mr. Amit Kapri, Advocate for the revisionist.
Mr. Lalit Miglani, Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand.
Dated: 07.09.2017
Honíble V.K. Bist, J.
The criminal revision has been filed by the
revisionist for quashing the judgment and order dated
21.08.2017 passed by the learned Sessions
Judge/Juvenile Judge, Pithoragarh in Criminal Appeal
No. 58 of 2017, Computer Generated No.
UKP1010002712017 ìBalwant Singh v. Stateí, whereby
the learned Sessions Judge/Juvenile Judge has
rejected the bail/custody of juvenile Balwant Singh to
his parents in Case Crime No. 08 of 2017, under
Section 306, 323, 504, 452/34 of I.P.C., Police Station
Gangolihat, District Pithoragarh.
2. Learned counsel for the revisionist
submitted that revisionist was arrested in connection
with Case Crime No. 08 of 2017, relating to offences
punishable under Section 306, 323, 504, 452/ 34 of
I.P.C. The revisionist moved the bail application before
the learned Sessions Judge/Juvenile Judge,
Pithoragarh; but, the same was rejected vide order
dated 21.08.2017. Learned counsel for the revisionist
argued that the learned Sessions Judge/Juvenile

2
Judge, while disposing of the appeal of the revisionist,
did not consider the gravity of the offence; rather, the
learned Sessions Judge/Juvenile Judge had to
consider the capability of the guardian. He also
submitted that in the statement of the only eye-witness, namely, Smt. Bhawana Devi, recorded under
Section 164 Cr.P.C. did not disclose any specific role of
the revisionist in the commission of the alleged crime.
3. Section 12 (1) of the Juvenile Justice (Care
and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, provides that
when any person, who is apparently a child and is
alleged to have committed a bailable or non-bailable
offence, is apprehended or detained by the police or
appears or brought before a Board, such person shall,
notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of
Criminal Procedure, 1973 or in any other law for the
time being in force, be released on bail with or without
surety or placed under the supervision of a Probation
Officer or under the care of any fit person:
 Provided that such person shall not be so
released if there appears reasonable grounds for
believing that the release is likely to bring that person
into association with any known criminal or expose the
said person to moral, physical or psychological danger
or the personís release would defeat the ends of justice,
and the Board shall record the reasons for denying the
bail and circumstances that led to such a decision.
4. Thus, as per Section 12 (1) of the Act, the
revisionist shall be subject to the condition mentioned
in the Act. In the present case, admittedly, the

3
revisionist is a Juvenile. Learned counsel for the
revisionist submitted that the family members of the
revisionist have no criminal history. Parents of the
revisionist are ready to keep revisionist with them and
are ready to give undertaking.
5. Considering the facts and circumstances of
the case, the revision is allowed. Impugned judgment
and order dated 21.08.2017 passed by learned
Sessions Judge/Juvenile Judge in Criminal Appeal No.
58 of 2017 is set aside.
6. Let revisionist Balwant Singh be released on
bail on executing personal bond and furnishing two
sureties each of the like amount by his natural
guardian and father to the satisfaction of learned
Sessions Judge/Juvenile Judge, Pithoragarh. His
father shall also submit an undertaking that the
Juvenile will remain in his custody.
 (V.K. Bist, J.)
 07.09.2017
Navin
